new_findings.title: Fingerprint labels the cv2 version as the resolved OpenCV wheel
new_findings.defect: resolved_versions maps opencv-python to self.opencv_version, which comes from cv2.__version__. In this checkout cv2 reports 5.0.0 while uv.lock resolves opencv-python 5.0.0.93, so the advertised exact resolved version and comparison token omit the wheel build version.
new_findings.failure_scenario: If a deployment changes from opencv-python 5.0.0.93 to another 5.0.0.* wheel while cv2.__version__ remains 5.0.0, run snapshots keep the same OpenCV version and comparison token despite a changed resolved package.
new_findings.fix: Record importlib.metadata.version('opencv-python') in resolved_versions (and the active opencv-python-headless distribution when installed); retain cv2.__version__ as a separate runtime field and include the resolved distribution identity in comparability_token.

summary: All five assigned findings hold; the residual MediaIdentity concern is refuted because the ORM and schema expose quality_score used by ensure_matview. A medium OpenCV wheel-version fingerprint gap remains, and the lane test run is blocked by an aiosqlite fixture timeout after uv required the no-sync fallback.
